interest: For historians of prewar Japan and U.S.-Japan relations, this docket sheet highlights the U.S. government's surveillance of Japanese civic and youth mobilization during the militarizing period of the mid-1930s. Although the underlying report is not bound with this sheet, the entry confirms that the U.S. Military Attaché in Tokyo actively investigated the Seinendan (Young Men's Association), an organization central to state-sponsored youth indoctrination, physical training, and patriotic citizenship. Additionally, it illustrates the State Department's decimal classification system (894.408) for categorizing foreign civic, social, and citizenship organizations.
overview: This file consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet for U.S. State Department decimal file 894.408, classified under 'Social Matters: Japan - Organizations In Interest Of Better Citizenship. Americanization.' The sheet registers a single entry, Sub No. 1, recording report #7560 dated November 24, 1934, from the U.S. Military Attaché in Japan. The recorded report describes the purpose, membership, and activities of the Japanese Young Men's Association (Seinendan); the underlying report text itself is not included in the file bundle.

subfiles.about: A State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet indexing incoming documentation concerning Japanese citizenship and youth organizations under decimal file 894.408.
subfiles.summary: This single-page List of Papers indexes State Department file 894.408 regarding organizations in the interest of better citizenship in Japan. It registers an incoming report (Sub No. 1 / Report #7560) from the U.S. Military Attaché in Japan dated November 24, 1934. The recorded purport indicates that the report submitted details on the purpose, membership, and activities of the Young Men's Association (Seinendan).
